items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: he picked up me and my brother, Gus, and Roy Eldridge from Detroit and took us down to his home town in Muncie, Indiana... we spent oh, a couple of weeks down there in Muncie rehearsing

ctx.x: What did your mother and father teach? The subjects.

My father was the Dean there, the Dean of Men, I believe his job was -- and my mother taught in the elementary grades, and she taught my brother, Gus -- and me, to read and write at home, so we actually entered school in the second grade when we were about four years old, because she had taught us all that material, and in the south, in those days, there was nothing compulsory about having to be six years old to go in the first grade.

items.title: 68154_Gus Johnson oral history interview
items.q: I heard Teddy with the big bands.

ctx.x: Because that was so far ahead of what everybody was doing on piano, wasn't it?
Earl and later I think it was Teddy Wilson.
Oh, but you heard Tatum first.
